# livck_recurring_maintenance (Resource)

A maintenance window that repeats on a schedule, for example every night from 02:00 to 03:00. While a window runs, the covered services raise no incidents and send no alerts, and the linked status pages show the maintenance. Windows open and close on their own; the computed attributes (`state`, `next_start_at`, `next_end_at`, `rule_text`) follow them and never cause a diff.

Exceptions (skipping or moving single windows) are not part of this resource. Manage them in the console or through the API; they do not cause a diff here.

Destroying the resource deletes the recurring maintenance. A window running at that moment ends right away and monitoring resumes; past windows stay in the history.

With an API token restricted to access areas, the API lists only the services and status pages of those areas. A configuration that names others then shows a diff on every plan; use a token without area restrictions for maintenances that span areas.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "livck_tag" "nightly_backup" {
  key   = "backup"
  value = "nightly"
}

# Every night from 02:00 to 03:00 Berlin time, for every service that carries
# the tag when the window starts. Times stay local across daylight saving.
resource "livck_recurring_maintenance" "nightly_backup" {
  title_translations = {
    en = "Nightly backup"
    de = "Nächtliche Sicherung"
  }
  timezone = "Europe/Berlin"

  schedule {
    frequency        = "daily"
    anchor_date      = "2026-12-01"
    start_time       = "02:00"
    duration_minutes = 60
  }

  tag_ids        = [livck_tag.nightly_backup.id]
  statuspage_ids = [livck_statuspage.main.id]
  notify_start   = true
}

# Patch day: the second Tuesday of every month, 22:00 to 23:30, until the end
# of 2027, for two services picked by hand.
resource "livck_recurring_maintenance" "patch_day" {
  title    = "Patch day"
  timezone = "Europe/Berlin"

  schedule {
    frequency        = "monthly"
    anchor_date      = "2026-12-01"
    start_time       = "22:00"
    duration_minutes = 90
    until_date       = "2027-12-31"

    month {
      mode    = "nth_weekday"
      nth     = 2
      weekday = 2
    }
  }

  service_ids = [livck_service.website.id, livck_service.api.id]
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `timezone` (String) IANA time zone the times of `schedule` are meant in, e.g. `Europe/Berlin`. Windows keep their local time across daylight saving changes.

### Optional

- `description_translations` (Map of String) Optional description per language. Removing it from the configuration removes it.
- `notify_end` (Boolean) Notify the subscribers of the linked status pages when a window ends. Defaults to `false`.
- `notify_start` (Boolean) Notify the subscribers of the linked status pages when a window starts. Defaults to `false`.
- `paused` (Boolean) Pause by hand: no window starts until it is set back to `false`, and a window running at that moment ends. Defaults to `false`. A pause caused by the plan limit is not reflected here (see `paused_reason`) and cannot be lifted from Terraform.
- `schedule` (Block, Optional) The rule. Required. Stored exactly as written, so it never drifts. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--schedule))
- `service_ids` (Set of String) Services the windows cover (public ids), at most 400. Left out, the selection is not managed by Terraform and stays as set in the console.
- `statuspage_ids` (Set of String) Status pages that show the maintenance (public ids), at most 50. Without any, it stays internal. Left out, the selection is not managed by Terraform.
- `tag_ids` (Set of String) Tags (public ids), at most 20. Every service carrying one of them when a window starts is covered. Left out, the selection is not managed by Terraform.
- `title` (String) Single-language title, stored in the organization's default language. Exactly one of `title` and `title_translations` must be set. An import reads the title as `title_translations`; with `title` in the configuration, the next apply writes it once.
- `title_translations` (Map of String) Title per language as a `{locale = value}` map, e.g. `{ de = "Nächtliche Sicherung", en = "Nightly backup" }`. Exactly one of `title` and `title_translations` must be set.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The ID of this resource.
- `next_end_at` (String) End of the running or the next window (RFC 3339). Null when paused or ended.
- `next_start_at` (String) Start of the running or the next window (RFC 3339). Null when paused or ended.
- `paused_reason` (String) Why it is paused: `manual`, `plan_limit` (more recurring maintenances than the plan allows; upgrade, and it resumes on its own) or `org_deleted`. Null when not paused.
- `rule_text` (String) The schedule in plain words, for display.
- `state` (String) `idle` (waiting for the next window), `running` (a window runs right now), `paused` or `ended` (the schedule has no further window).

<a id="nestedblock--schedule"></a>
### Nested Schema for `schedule`

Required:

- `anchor_date` (String) First day the rule applies (`YYYY-MM-DD`). With an interval above 1 it also fixes which days, weeks or months count.
- `duration_minutes` (Number) Length of a window in minutes, 5 to 10080 (seven days), shorter than the gap between two windows.
- `frequency` (String) `daily`, `weekly` or `monthly`.
- `start_time` (String) Local start time as `HH:MM` (24 hours) in `timezone`.

Optional:

- `interval` (Number) Every n days, weeks or months, 1 to 99. Defaults to `1`.
- `month` (Block, Optional) Monthly only, and required there. Either `mode = "day"` with `day`, or `mode = "nth_weekday"` with `nth` and `weekday`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--schedule--month))
- `until_date` (String) Last day a window may start (`YYYY-MM-DD`, inclusive). Without it the rule repeats forever.
- `weekdays` (Set of Number) Weekly only, and required there: the days of the week, `0` = Sunday, `1` = Monday … `6` = Saturday.

<a id="nestedblock--schedule--month"></a>
### Nested Schema for `schedule.month`

Optional:

- `day` (String) For `day`: `1` to `31`, or `last`. A month without that day has no window.
- `mode` (String) `day` (a day of the month) or `nth_weekday` (e.g. the last Sunday).
- `nth` (String) For `nth_weekday`: `1` to `4`, or `last`.
- `weekday` (Number) For `nth_weekday`: `0` = Sunday … `6` = Saturday.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import livck_recurring_maintenance.nightly_backup <recurring_maintenance_public_id>
```
